behavioral_health_services_tax.source: 2025 Personal Income Tax Booklet (Form 540), instructions for Form 540, line 62 -- Behavioral Health Services Tax: if taxable income (line 19) is more than $1,000,000, the tax is 1% of the excess over $1,000,000, figured in whole dollars (renamed from the Mental Health Services Tax for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025).

brackets.source: 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules, 2025 Personal Income Tax Booklet (Form 540), p. 75: Schedule X (single or married/RDP filing separately), Schedule Y (married/RDP filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse/RDP), Schedule Z (head of household). Marginal rates 1.00% / 2.00% / 4.00% / 6.00% / 8.00% / 9.30% / 10.30% / 11.30% / 12.30% for every schedule; the printed base amounts at each threshold are exactly the cumulative marginal tax of the thresholds (verified during the tax-table extraction). Used only above $100,000 of taxable income; at or below it the 2025 California Tax Table (params/2025-ca-tax-table.json) applies.

caleitc.source: 2025 California Earned Income Tax Credit Booklet (FTB 3514), Franchise Tax Board, https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-3514-booklet.pdf: Step 1, question a -- federal AGI (federal Form 1040, line 11) must be less than $32,901. Step 2, Worksheet 1, line 13 -- investment income (federal lines 2a + 2b + 3b + the floored capital gain of line 7, in v1 scope) must not exceed $4,814. Step 6, California Earned Income Tax Credit Worksheet, Part II -- when federal AGI differs from California earned income, the AGI lookup applies unless AGI is less than $4,661 (no qualifying children), $6,998 (one qualifying child), or $9,823 (two or more qualifying children). Step 4, question b -- a filer without a qualifying child must be at least age 18 at the end of 2025, i.e. born on or before January 1, 2008 (the form's own wording); no filer age test applies on the with-children path (Step 3). Earned income: Step 5 -- form FTB 3514 line 13 is W-2 box 16 California wages; line 18 business income is Worksheet 3 (federal Schedule 1 line 3 business income minus line 4, the deductible part of self-employment tax from federal Schedule 1 line 15). Credit amounts come from the 2025 Earned Income Tax Credit Table (params/2025-ca-eitc-table.json).

exemption_credits.source: Form 540 (2025), Side 1, lines 7-11, printed on the form (2025 Personal Income Tax Booklet, form pages): line 7 personal, line 8 blind, and line 9 senior (65 or older) exemptions are $153 each; line 10 dependents are $475 each; line 11 is the sum, transferred to line 32. Phaseout: booklet instructions for line 32, 'Exemption Credits' and the AGI Limitation Worksheet that follows it -- if federal AGI (Form 540, line 13) exceeds $252,203 (single or married/RDP filing separately), $504,411 (married/RDP filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse/RDP), or $378,310 (head of household), the excess is divided by $2,500 ($1,250 if married/RDP filing separately), rounded up to the next whole number, multiplied by $6, and that per-exemption reduction is applied separately to the combined lines 7-9 credits (scaled by the count of lines 7+8+9 exemptions) and to the line 10 dependent credits (scaled by the dependent count), each floored at zero.

standard_deduction.source: 2025 Personal Income Tax Booklet (Form 540), Franchise Tax Board, 'California Standard Deduction Chart for Most People' (instructions for Form 540, line 18), https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-booklet.pdf: single $5,706; married/RDP filing jointly $11,412; married/RDP filing separately $5,706; head of household $11,412 (qualifying surviving spouse/RDP $11,412, not a v1 filing status). California gives no standard-deduction addition for age 65 or blindness; those facts instead earn exemption credits (see exemption_credits).

yctc.source: 2025 California Earned Income Tax Credit Booklet (FTB 3514), General Information ('the maximum amount of credit allowable for a qualified taxpayer is $1,189 and the credit amount phases out as earned income exceeds the threshold amount of $27,425, and completely phases out at $32,901') and Step 8 / form FTB 3514 Part VII, lines 23-28: the taxpayer must have been allowed the California EITC (or would have been allowed it but for earned income of zero or less, subject to the line 23a/23b gates: total wages and total net losses each not in excess of $35,640, and federal AGI not in excess of $32,900) and have a qualifying child (for the California EITC) who is younger than six years old as of the last day of the taxable year. Line 24 is $1,189; if California earned income (line 23) exceeds $27,425, the excess is divided by 100 (two decimal places, not rounded) and multiplied by $21.71 to get the reduction (lines 25-27); the credit is line 24 minus line 27, entered as $1 when it falls between $0 and $1 and rounded to the nearest whole dollar when over $1 (line 28). The credit is per return, not per child, and is entered on Form 540, line 76.
